title: The arithmetical hierarchy and alternating searches

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §16.1, printed/PDF pp. 67–68, Definition 16.1, Proposition 16.2, Exercise 16.3, Proposition 16.4 and Lemma 16.5(1–4)

summary: Classify relations by alternating quantifiers over computable tests, prove closure properties, and connect the ordinary positive levels with arithmetic formulas.
abstract: Saying that a program eventually answers every input allows a different finite wait for each input. Reversing the order of these demands would ask for one bound that works everywhere. The arithmetical hierarchy organizes such distinctions by counting alternating existential and universal quantifiers over a terminating membership test. Finite lists collect the separate witnesses needed by bounded families without adding another alternation. At the first level, an existential description is exactly recognition by a program; two complementary descriptions give a decision procedure. These results also hold when the tests may query a fixed oracle. For ordinary computable tests, the positive levels agree with the corresponding quantifier patterns in arithmetic formulas, giving compatible algorithmic and logical descriptions of properties such as totality and finiteness.
